A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TriDi and contain complete, readable main papers and supplementary Sections 7–13. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, qualitative experiments, and a user study with 40 responses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a COINS comparison and quantitative penetration analysis in Tables S3 and S8.

M1.justification: The trilateral diffusion architecture, contact-text representation, losses, augmentation, guidance, and optional hand refinement are unchanged. SDFit is suggested as possible upstream mesh reconstruction, without an implemented modification to TriDi.

E1.justification: The datasets, application domains, and seven conditioning modes are retained. The COINS comparison evaluates the existing human-generation-from-object-and-interaction mode on BEHAVE; it introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds COINS as an evaluated comparator for BEHAVE human generation conditioned on object and text in Table S3. Existing comparisons remain. CHOIS and DiffH2O are cited as metric sources, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds SDF-based minimum-distance, contact-percentage, penetration-depth, and penetration-score evaluation, and distribution/pose-error scoring for the COINS comparison. Section 5.3 also revises the reported keyframe sampling rate from 1 to 2 fps. Existing training and dataset-split protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 9 and Table S8 add a focused analysis of contact, floating objects, and interpenetration on BEHAVE and GRAB. Existing component ablations, template analysis, unseen-object examples, and refinement demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report distribution statistics across three sampling runs and retain the same uncertainty reporting and user-study sample size. The new COINS table uses the existing plus/minus reporting convention; no new statistical procedure or increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and matched supplementary-table values are unchanged. New Table S3 reports BEHAVE H|O,I MPJPE of 16.9 cm for TriDi versus 43.4 for COINS. Table S8 adds contact and penetration results, including mixed rankings on GRAB.

T1.justification: Equations 1–29, diffusion formulations, loss definitions, and refinement derivations are unchanged. The added empirical metric descriptions introduce no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint HOI modeling, seven operating modes, the contact-text representation, baseline advantages, and applications. The new evaluations support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation of COINS struggling beyond sitting interactions and suggests SDFit to relax the known-mesh requirement. It also claims favorable penetration behavior, although Table S8 shows mixed penetration rankings on GRAB. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 revises sequence-construction instructions to use 2 fps keyframes instead of 1 fps, retaining spherical rotation interpolation and linear translation interpolation. Architecture details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and code-release information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, including COINS, DiffH2O, SDFit, PICO, and InteractVLM, with limited updates to existing positioning. The new penetration paragraph incorrectly labels reference [109], identified elsewhere as COINS, as CHOIS.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits in the baseline and application descriptions and short new evaluation paragraphs in Section 9. The main narrative, section sequence, and supplementary organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables S3 and S8; former Tables S3–S6 become S4–S7. Some supplementary tables change width and placement, and the title block and text reflow. Existing figures and illustrated samples are retained.

improvement.justification: The COINS comparison and direct contact/penetration measurements modestly strengthen evidence beyond v2's existing evaluations. The gains are limited by sparse new experimental details, a metric-source citation error, and overbroad penetration interpretation: on GRAB, TriDi improves contact rates but has worse penetration-depth scores than the baselines. The underlying method and established results remain intact.
